messages:
alice-support: Heads-up: customer (acct 7632) is seeing intermittent 401s when calling Redwood from a Vercel Edge route. They say Authorization header is present at ingress but missing by the time the edge runtime calls the API. Attaching ticket + repro link: https://repro.example/ve-401.

bob-cust: repro details: Next.js middleware proxies to /api/ai using fetch. SDK version @redwood/inference 0.8.2 (edge build). Node local works fine, only Vercel Edge fails. Example middleware:```js
// middleware.ts
export async function middleware(req) {
  // forward auth to internal API
  const token = req.headers.get('authorization')
  await fetch(new URL('/api/ai', req.url), { headers: { authorization: token } })
}
```

bob-cust: logs from Vercel edge (incoming request shows auth):
```
INGRESS: authorization: Bearer abc123
EDGE_FETCH_OUTGOING: authorization: <missing>
```

alice-support: Is this a preflight/CORS issue or header trimming by the platform? Does Vercel show any rewrite docs?

carmen-eng: Likely not browser CORS — this is server-side inside the Edge runtime. Vercel sometimes strips sensitive headers when routing to internal next routes (e.g., internal rewrites/edges). Can you confirm whether you're using a relative URL ("/api/ai") vs absolute (https://your.app/api/ai)? Relative may trigger internal routing that rewrites headers.

bob-cust: We used relative url. Switching to full origin in local test still failed. Also tried adding `credentials: 'include'` but no change.

carmen-eng: Two quick things to try: 1) instead of relying on Authorization being forwarded automatically, explicitly copy it to a custom header inside middleware (e.g., x-forwarded-authorization) and read that in your API route. 2) Confirm the runtime isn't cloning the Request in a way that drops headers. Example workaround:```js
// middleware.ts
export async function middleware(req) {
  const token = req.headers.get('authorization')
  const url = new URL('/api/ai', req.url)
  await fetch(url.toString(), { headers: { 'x-forwarded-authorization': token } })
}
```

bob-cust: Added x-forwarded-authorization and API reads it -> auth works. But customer unhappy because they expect direct Authorization passthrough. Also noticed a billing spike — the SDK is retrying on 401 and hammering the backend when auth fails. Any idea on retry behavior?

dave-devex: Thanks — two separate issues: header preservation in Vercel edge routing (platform) and retry logic in the SDK. We shipped a header-preserve fix on the SDK edge client in 0.9.0 that addresses Request cloning that could drop headers in some edge runtimes. Recommend upgrading from 0.8.2 -> 0.9.0. Commit: https://git.internal/rdw/edge-fixes/commit/abcde123.

dave-devex: For retries: by default the SDK will do limited idempotent retries for network errors and some 5xxs; 401 should NOT be retried but earlier client only checked presence of body/timeout and retried incorrectly in edge when Authorization was absent. 0.9.0 also toggles stricter retry gating. As a short-term workaround set retries to 0:```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, retries: 0 })
```

bob-cust: Reproduced locally with 0.9.0 pre-release — Authorization now preserved when using absolute URL. With relative URL still flaky on Vercel edge internal route. Customer wants guidance for production on Vercel.

carmen-eng: If you must use relative routes (internal rewrites), keep using x-forwarded-authorization; otherwise use absolute origin and upgrade SDK. Also add a small middleware change to avoid double fetches on error: only call SDK once and bubble errors instead of retrying in middleware.

bob-cust: Noted. Also attached small repro steps for SRE: 1) deploy branch `ve-401-debug` to Vercel, 2) curl the edge route with Bearer header, 3) watch logs for outgoing fetch headers. Repo: https://repro.example/ve-401.git

alice-support: Action items: - ask customer if they can upgrade to 0.9.0 (we'll offer to patch their project) - suggest using absolute URL or x-forwarded-authorization as workaround - provide billing mitigation: set SDK retries=0 and we'll investigate billing credits for duplicated calls.

deploy-bot: Deployment started for ve-401-debug at https://vercel.example/deploy/ve-401-debug (build 715) :rocket:

carmen-eng: I'll open an internal bug to track platform header-handling behavior on Vercel edge rewrites; link: https://issues.internal/PLAT-942. Will sync with Vercel if needed.

alice-support: I'll follow up with the customer with the workaround + offer to help upgrade. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
